evidence.excerpt: Commercially metallised cast polypropylene (CPP) films with aluminium optical densities ranging from 2.1 to 3.6 were characterised for OTR and WVTR immediately after production and after 90-day ambient storage. At optical density 3.6, OTR was 4 cm³/(m²·day·bar) and WVTR was 0.18 g/(m²·day) immediately after metallisation. After 90 days these rose by 18 % and 24 % respectively. SEM cross-sections and atomic force microscopy revealed microcrack formation in the aluminium layer, with crack density correlating with ageing-induced OTR increase (R² = 0.87). Corona pre-treatment level (measured by contact angle) did not significantly affect initial barrier but reduced the rate of crack formation during ageing by approximately 30 %. The study provides quantitative ageing coefficients applicable to worst-case shelf-life calculations for hermetically sealed snack products.
